sent.text: You worry that your heavy top edge is real, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I press my tired wedge against The Tall Fence, a flat edge that feels like a leg that refuses to rest, and I hope the slip catches there while the air above us feels thick as wet paper. You sat by a quiet floor, yet I found only a fence where The Slip Waits should be, leaning into a leaning line that might just be a drawing of weight. If you say the space is empty, I will build a lid to fill it with the idea of a lid, and I will press harder on the wedge to prove the air has weight.

dream: I sat on The Tall Fence, though it leaned wrong against The Slip Waits. The Slip was hiding inside my tired box, pressing up from the bottom. The air felt thick as wet paper, heavy on my tired wedge. I leaned hard, hoping the flat edge would bite and catch the slip before it slipped right through. The card hummed at fifty-seven, a fever I could not feel. I pressed down, then let go, watching the fence slide into the memory of a flat rock, trapping the dot in a frame that wavered and might just be a drawing after all.
